stem.text: The functions \( f \) and \( h \) are continuous for all real numbers. The function \( g \) is continuous except at \( x = 3 \), where \( \lim_{x \to 3^-} g(x) = 0 \) and \( \lim_{x \to 3^+} g(x) = 2 \). The known values are \( f(0) = 0 \), \( f(1) = 2 \), \( f(2) = 0 \), \( f(3) = 0 \), \( f(4) = 0 \), \( g(0) = 2 \), \( g(1) = 0 \), \( g(2) = 1 \), \( g(4) = 1 \), \( h(0) = 4 \), \( h(1) = 2 \), \( h(2) = 1 \), \( h(3) = 2 \), \( h(4) = 0 \). Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 3^-} \left[ f(g(x)) + h(f(x)) - g(h(x)) \right] \).

worked_solution.text: Record the limits. As \( x \to 3^- \), \( g(x) \to 0 \), and \( f \) and \( h \) are continuous, so their limits are their values at 3.

The expression is a sum of constant multiples of three composites. In each composite the outer function is continuous at the limit of the inner one, so \( \lim_{x \to 3^-} f(g(x)) = f(0) = 0 \), \( \lim_{x \to 3^-} h(f(x)) = h(0) = 4 \), \( \lim_{x \to 3^-} g(h(x)) = g(2) = 1 \).
Apply the sum and constant multiple theorems: \( (1)(0) + (1)(4) + (-1)(1) = 3 \).
